title: Show HN: Capy-flash——基于两块16 GB消费级GPU的125B MoE模型
content:
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B MoE) in NVFP4 on two 16 GB consumer GPUs.
Against Strata 0.1.44.1 on the same machine (2x RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB, Ryzen 9 9900X, 96 GB DDR5):
- NVIDIA's official NVFP4 experts, used as published: not re-quantized.
- Fewer tokens, same finish time: Strata's 3-bit experts generate faster, but on the same coding tasks they write 23 % more tokens, so the agent finishes in the same time.
- Built for agents: 20/20 multi-step coding tasks, 0 malformed tool calls in 1,124; OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API.
- One engine, two models: it also serves the dense Qwen3.8-27B, exactly as ninfer-tp2 v0.4.9 did.
¹ Same prompts as the Strata runs, new text each time (the n-gram (PLE) table rows come from disk). Since v0.5.2 the next chunk's rows are read while the GPUs run the current one; v0.5.3 keeps the rows' multipliers in RAM (the first chunk of ~15k new tokens waits 0.3-0.5 s instead of 0.8-1.3 s) and computes the router on tensor cores. ² Strata 0.1.43 (0.1.44 did not change its IQ3_S path); 5 multi-step coding tasks x 4 runs, OpenCode. Details below.
Quick start (2x RTX 50-series 16 GB, an AVX-512 CPU, ~70 GiB of free RAM, 135 GB of disk):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ValerioDolci/capy-flash/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --check   # can this machine run it?
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ValerioDolci/capy-flash/main/install.sh | bash               # release + model into ~/capy-flash
~/capy-flash/current/serve-flash-next.sh ~/capy-flash/models/flash-next/qwen3_8_flash_next_nvfp4_idxgdnq8.ninfer
curl -s localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"capy-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17*23?"}]}'                # from another shell
The installer checks GPUs, driver, AVX-512, RAM and disk and says what to fix, verifies every download, and prints
a test request; --model 27b installs Qwen3.8-27B instead, --dir picks another place. By hand: download a
release tarball and hf download Feyd89/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-capy-flash.
The routed experts that do not fit in VRAM live in host RAM and are computed on the CPU; everything else runs tensor-parallel on the two GPUs. capy-flash is ninfer-tp2, renamed at v0.5.0: the two-GPU tensor-parallel fork of Neroued/ninfer (v0.1-v0.4.9 under the old name); NOTICE lists every piece of prior work it builds on.
Status: v0.5.4 (2026-10-16). Built, tested and measured on one machine (below). Not affiliated with Qwen or NVIDIA.
- Tensor parallel over PCIe on two GPUs without peer-to-peer (pinned-host mailbox, FP32 partial sums).
- A cache of routed experts in VRAM, partitioned by expert id between the two GPUs; missing experts are computed on the CPU (AVX-512 NVFP4 kernel with the GPU's W4A4 activation quantization), inside the captured CUDA graph.
- MTP speculative decoding (K = 3, draft vocabulary shortlist), INT8 KV with an elastic KV / expert-slot budget up to
262,144 tokens, prefix cache across turns; OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible server (ninfer-serve).
- The same binary still serves the dense Qwen3.8-27B (NVFP4, entirely on the two GPUs) exactly like ninfer-tp2 v0.4.9.
- Context cache for agents (v0.5.4): a request reserves its prompt plus a 4,096-token window of KV and grows it as the
answer grows (a large max_tokens no longer pushes other conversations out of VRAM), and with two GPUs the cache can
keep evicted conversations in RAM (--host-kv-mib, --host-state-slots; on in --profile 27b with 8 GiB, off on
Flash-Next, whose experts already pin most of the RAM). On an agentic replay of Qwen3.8-27B (3 interleaved sessions
and 11 subagents, production flags, 4 lanes): median time to first token 2.14 → 0.98 s, prompt tokens served from
cache 67 → 78 %, prompt tokens recomputed −35 %, decode unchanged.
One machine: AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 96 GB DDR5-5600, 2x RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB on PCIe 5.0 x8 + x8 (no P2P), Ubuntu, CUDA 13.1. "GB300" below is the quality reference: NVIDIA's NVFP4 checkpoint served by vLLM on a GB300, same prompts, paired.
Quality (serving configuration of this README, v0.5.3, 2026-10-16):
v0.5.3 computes the router of prompt chunks on tensor cores, which sums in another order and can pick another expert
where two are tied; with the previous router (NINFER_QWEN4_ROUTER_MMA=0) the same gate gave 0.9780 / 0.8482 on the 2026-10-14 build.
Agentic replay (bench/capy_flash): 3 synthetic coding-agent sessions, 53 turns, prompts growing to ~81k tokens with ~90 % prefix reuse, 256 output tokens per turn, temperature 0. Same machine, same day:
Agent tasks: 5 multi-step coding tasks of a private task bank, 4 runs each, OpenCode with the model's sampling: 20/20 solved, 42.9k generated tokens per run (Strata 0.1.43 IQ3_S on the same tasks: 52.7k, 20/20; the GB300 reference: 26.5k), no malformed tool call in 1,124.
Prefill (same prompts on the three engines, server side, no prefix reuse): ~3.5k / ~15k / ~55k tokens: capy-flash v0.5.3 1,985 / 3,778 / 3,977 tok/s (2026-10-16; v0.5.2: 1,856 / 3,302 / 3,715; v0.5.1: 1,941 / 3,435 / 2,791); Strata 0.1.44.1 IQ3_S 1,745 / 2,906 / 4,037; Strata NVFP4 1,347 / 2,703 / 3,821 (2026-10-15).
Start: a cold start of the Flash-Next server takes 26-29 s here (v0.5.2: 56-141 s), most of it reading the 64.6 GiB of experts from disk.
Qwen3.8-27B (same machine, ninfer-tp2 v0.4.9 serving flags, agentic replay at temperature 0): the ninfer-tp2 gate gives the same golden ids, perplexity (4k 4.385905, 64k 4.133481) and greedy texts (60/60) as v0.4.9; replay TTFT 1.42 s, decode 171.2 tok/s, total 156 s (v0.4.9: 1.40 s, 172.2 tok/s, 154 s), the same token counts on all 53 turns.
Quality, prefill and start were measured on v0.5.3; the agentic replay and agent tasks on an internal build of 2026-10-14,
whose computation differs from v0.5.3 in one PLE table row (T155) and in the prompt router (T183, above); see the
development log, which explains every Tnn tag found in the sources.
Linux, CUDA 13.1, two sm_120 GPUs (RTX 50 series) with 16 GB, a CPU with AVX-512 (F/BW/VL, VNNI), and about 70 GiB of
free RAM: the routed experts are one 64.6 GiB page-locked host allocation. The server checks this at startup and
refuses with the numbers when it does not fit (NINFER_RAM_GUARD=0 starts anyway).
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120a \
  -DNINFER_BUILD_APPS=ON -DNINFER_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=OFF -DBUILD_TESTING=ON \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-13.1/bin/nvcc
ninja -C build apps/ninfer-serve
Or take the prebuilt tarball of a release (Ubuntu, sm_120a):
it has serve-flash-next.sh and serve-tp2.sh (27B) with the profiles of this README (tools/release).
Ready to serve: Feyd89/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-capy-flash
(126.6 GB, the artifact measured above, with its draft shortlist and SHA256SUMS; NVIDIA Open Model License together with
the Qwen Community License of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next):
hf download Feyd89/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-capy-flash --local-dir <dir>
Or convert nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 yourself in one command (artifact + MTP draft shortlist, same result):
python tools/capy_flash/convert.py --model <checkpoint dir> --out <dir>
It runs python -m tools.convert --recipe qwen3_8_flash_next_nvfp4_idxbf16_gdnq8 --components text,mtp (experts NVFP4
as published, indexer BF16, GDN Q8, about 5 minutes on a GPU, 118 GB) and tools/qwen4_draft_shortlist.py.
build/apps/ninfer-serve <dir>/qwen3_8_flash_next_nvfp4_idxgdnq8.ninfer --profile flash-next --port 8098 --model-id capy-flash
--profile flash-next is the configuration measured above (--tp 2 --devices 0,1 --kv-dtype int8 --elastic --max-context 262144 --max-concurrency 1 --spec mtp --draft-tokens 3); --profile 27b is the ninfer-tp2 one for
Qwen3.8-27B (with Vision; --no-vision for artifacts without it). Flags given on the command line override the
profile's, in any order (ninfer-serve --help lists both). To keep it running: a systemd unit and a llama-swap entry
in examples/serving.
Docker. docker/Dockerfile.rele

report.summary: 两块16GB消费级显卡跑125B MoE模型
report.background: 百B级MoE模型本地部署长期被显存卡死，125B 规模通常要数据中心级 GPU（如 GB300）。Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 是 Qwen 的 125B MoE 模型，NVIDIA 已放出官方 NVFP4 量化权重。作者 ValerioDolci 此前维护双卡张量并行推理框架 ninfer-tp2，capy-flash 即其 v0.5.0 起的改名版本：把放不进显存的专家层卸载到主机内存由 CPU 计算，其余在两张 RTX 5070 Ti 上张量并行，从而在消费级机器上跑通该模型并开源发布。
key_points: 显存不够就放内存：64.6 GiB 路由专家常驻主机内存，由 AVX-512 CPU 计算，其余部分双卡张量并行，专家按 id 分片缓存进两块 GPU 显存。
不依赖 NVLink 和 GPU 点对点：靠 PCIe 上的 pinned-host mailbox 传中间结果、FP32 部分和聚合，普通消费级主板也能双卡并跑。
为 Agent 而生：私有多步编码任务 20/20 全部通过，1124 次工具调用零格式错误，同时兼容 OpenAI 与 Anthropic 接口，可直接接 OpenCode。
速度与质量兼顾：55k token 预填约 3977 tok/s，超过同机 Strata IQ3_S；专家权重直接用 NVIDIA 官方 NVFP4 未重量化，冷启动仅 26-29 秒。
硬件门槛清晰：需 AVX-512 CPU、约 70 GiB 空闲内存、135 GB 磁盘，安装脚本会先体检并提示该修什么，不达标会带数字拒绝启动。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业，它证明消费级硬件加异构 CPU/GPU 卸载足以承载百B级 MoE，动摇了“必须上数据中心 GPU”的默认假设，也让量化与专家卸载成为竞争焦点。对开发者，一张 96GB 内存的家用工作站即可本地跑强模型，API 兼容意味着现有 agent 代码几乎无需改动，但 AVX-512 与 70GB 内存的门槛仍不低。对普通用户，短期仍是极客玩具，却会推动本地推理和隐私化部署继续下沉。
report.tools: 关注 GitHub 仓库 ValerioDolci/capy-flash 及上游 Neroued/ninfer；权重在 Hugging Face 的 Feyd89/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-capy-flash；一键脚本 install.sh 支持 --check 预检与 --model 27b 切换；examples/serving 提供 systemd 与 llama-swap 配置，便于接入 agent 工具链。
